dedupe_keys.name: hse urgent and emergency care report ireland formerly trolleygar daily 8am count of patients on trolleys delayed transfers and surge capacity by hospital

description: This daily report is the Irish health service's own measure of hospital crowding: how many admitted patients are waiting on trolleys in emergency departments and wards each morning, how many are delayed in leaving hospital, and how much surge capacity is in use. It is published by the Health Service Executive, which runs Ireland's public hospitals, and replaced the earlier TrolleyGAR report. Coverage is Ireland's public hospitals, reported at 8am each day as a national summary with hospital figures, with past days available through a date picker. Figures include patients on trolleys in emergency departments and in wards, those waiting more than 24 hours and those over 75 waiting more than 24 hours, delayed transfers of care counted at midnight, and surge beds in use reported at 2pm; for 25 September 2026 the national total was 325 patients on trolleys. The report is free and available on the web, but there is no download or open licence, so a series must be compiled day by day. Caveats: it is a snapshot at one time of day, surge capacity is only added later in the day, and figures are counts, not capacities. Simulation uses: calibrating hospital bed pressure and emergency department boarding in patient flow and winter surge models. Related records: the NHS trust classification (data-nhs-trust-classification-england) and the Quebec emergency department data (data-quebec-emergency-department-data) support similar crowding analyses elsewhere.
licence: HSE website terms (no open licence stated)

sources.note: Urgent and emergency care report (daily), previously TrolleyGAR: status of hospitals every day at 8am; people on trolleys in ED and in wards, delayed discharges, surge capacity use; date picker for past days; national summary 8am 25/09/2026: 229 on trolleys in EDs, 96 in wards, 325 total, 50 waiting more than 24 hours, 2 over-75s waiting more than 24 hours, 591 delayed transfers of care at midnight, surge capacity in use 510 (reported at 2pm); used to monitor ED admissions against each hospital's agreed threshold
